3	description: Jetpack Compose patterns for declarative UI, state management, theming, animations, and performance optimization.
4	---
5	
6	# Jetpack Compose Patterns
7	
8	Modern declarative UI patterns for Android.
9	
10	## State Management
11	
12	### State Hoisting
13	
14	```kotlin
15	// ✅ CORRECT: Stateless composable
16	@Composable
17	fun Counter(
18	    count: Int,
19	    onIncrement: () -> Unit,
20	    modifier: Modifier = Modifier
21	) {
22	    Row(modifier = modifier) {
23	        Text("Count: $count")
24	        Button(onClick = onIncrement) {
25	            Text("+")
26	        }
27	    }
28	}
29	
30	// Parent owns state
31	@Composable
32	fun CounterScreen() {
33	    var count by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(0) }
34	    
35	    Counter(
36	        count = count,
37	        onIncrement = { count++ }
38	    )
39	}
40	```
41	
42	### Remember Variants
43	
44	```kotlin
45	// remember - Survives recomposition
46	val alpha by remember { mutableStateOf(1f) }
47	
48	// rememberSaveable - Survives config change
49	var count by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(0) }
50	
51	// remember with key - Resets on key change
52	val animation = remember(itemId) { Animatable(0f) }
53	
54	// derivedStateOf - Computed, updates only when result changes
55	val isValid by remember {
56	    derivedStateOf { email.isNotBlank() && password.length >= 8 }
57	}
58	```
59	
60	## Composition Patterns
61	
62	### Slot API
63	
64	```kotlin
65	@Composable
66	fun AppBar(
67	    title: @Composable () -> Unit,
68	    navigationIcon: @Composable () -> Unit = {},
69	    actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit = {}
70	) {
71	    TopAppBar(
72	        title = { title() },
73	        navigationIcon = { navigationIcon() },
74	        actions = actions
75	    )
76	}
77	
78	// Usage
79	AppBar(
80	    title = { Text("Home") },
81	    navigationIcon = { IconButton(onClick = {}) { Icon(Icons.Default.Menu, null) } },
82	    actions = {
83	        IconButton(onClick = {}) { Icon(Icons.Default.Search, null) }
84	    }
85	)
86	```
87	
88	### Modifier Pattern
89	
90	```kotlin
91	@Composable
92	fun CustomButton(
93	    onClick: () -> Unit,
94	    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,  // First optional parameter
95	    enabled: Boolean = true,
96	    content: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit
97	) {
98	    Button(
99	        onClick = onClick,
100	        modifier = modifier,  // Apply modifier first
101	        enabled = enabled,
102	        content = content
103	    )
104	}
105	```

107	## Side Effects
108	
109	### LaunchedEffect
110	
111	```kotlin
112	@Composable
113	fun HomeScreen(viewModel: HomeViewModel) {
114	    // Runs once
115	    LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
116	        viewModel.loadData()
117	    }
118	    
119	    // Runs when key changes
120	    LaunchedEffect(userId) {
121	        viewModel.loadUser(userId)
122	    }
123	}
124	```
125	
126	### DisposableEffect
127	
128	```kotlin
129	@Composable
130	fun LifecycleObserver(onResume: () -> Unit) {
131	    val lifecycleOwner = LocalLifecycleOwner.current
132	    
133	    DisposableEffect(lifecycleOwner) {
134	        val observer = LifecycleEventObserver { _, event ->
135	            if (event == Lifecycle.Event.ON_RESUME) onResume()
136	        }
137	        lifecycleOwner.lifecycle.addObserver(observer)
138	        
139	        onDispose {
140	            lifecycleOwner.lifecycle.removeObserver(observer)
141	        }
142	    }
143	}
144	```

146	## Theming
147	
148	### Material 3
149	
150	```kotlin
151	@Composable
152	fun AppTheme(
153	    darkTheme: Boolean = isSystemInDarkTheme(),
154	    content: @Composable () -> Unit
155	) {
156	    val colorScheme = if (darkTheme) DarkColorScheme else LightColorScheme
157	    
158	    MaterialTheme(
159	        colorScheme = colorScheme,
160	        typography = AppTypography,
161	        content = content
162	    )
163	}
164	
165	// Usage
166	val backgroundColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface
167	val textStyle = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge
168	```

171	
172	### LazyColumn
173	
174	```kotlin
175	LazyColumn {
176	    items(
177	        items = users,
178	        key = { it.id }  // Critical for performance
179	    ) { user ->
180	        UserItem(user = user)
181	    }
182	}
183	```
184	
185	## Animations
186	
187	### Animate Values
188	
189	```kotlin
190	val alpha by animateFloatAsState(
191	    targetValue = if (visible) 1f else 0f,
192	    animationSpec = tween(durationMillis = 300)
193	)
194	
195	val size by animateDpAsState(
196	    targetValue = if (expanded) 200.dp else 100.dp
197	)
198	```
199	
200	### AnimatedContent
201	
202	```kotlin
203	AnimatedContent(
204	    targetState = state,
205	    transitionSpec = {
206	        fadeIn() togetherWith fadeOut()
207	    }
208	) { targetState ->
209	    when (targetState) {
210	        is Loading -> LoadingContent()
211	        is Success -> SuccessContent(targetState.data)
212	        is Error -> ErrorContent()
213	    }
214	}
215	```

5	
6	# Compose: slot API pattern
7	
8	## Core principle
9	
10	A reusable Compose component describes layout structure. Callers provide variable visual content through slots.
11	
12	## API review procedure
13	
14	1. Confirm the component is reusable. For a true single-use composable, do not add slot ceremony.
15	2. Mark which regions vary by caller: headline, supporting text, leading visual, trailing visual, actions, body.
16	3. Replace caller-controlled primitive content and shape flags with slots.
17	4. Add receiver scopes only when the slot is emitted inside a layout whose scope APIs callers should use.
18	5. Make absent optional regions nullable (`null`), so the component can omit their containers and spacing.
19	6. Put repeated default content or tokens in `XxxDefaults`.
20	7. Pair this with the `modifier` rules in `compose-modifier-and-layout-style`.
21	
22	## 1. Replace primitive content with `@Composable` slots
23	
24	Where the component asks for caller-controlled *content*, prefer a `@Composable () -> Unit` slot. Where the slot is structurally required, leave it non-nullable with no default. Where it's optional, make it nullable with a `null` default.
25	
26	```kotlin
27	// ❌ BAD — primitive parameters; trailing area is the only slot; everything else is locked
28	@Composable
29	fun SettingsRow(
30	    title: String,
31	    onClick: () -> Unit,
32	    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
33	    subtitle: String? = null,
34	    leadingIcon: ImageVector? = null,
35	    trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
36	) { … }
37	```
38	
39	```kotlin
40	// ✅ GOOD — every visual region is a slot; the row describes structure, not content
41	@Composable
42	fun SettingsRow(
43	    headlineContent: @Composable () -> Unit,
44	    onClick: () -> Unit,
45	    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
46	    supportingContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
47	    leadingContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
48	    trailingContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
49	) { … }
50	```
51	
52	Call sites stay short when the typical content is a one-liner:
53	
54	```kotlin
55	SettingsRow(
56	    headlineContent = { Text("Account") },
57	    leadingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.Person, contentDescription = null) },
58	    trailingContent = { SettingsRowDefaults.Chevron() },
59	    onClick = { … },
60	)
61	```
62	
63	The unusual cases no longer require new component parameters:
64	
65	```kotlin
66	SettingsRow(
67	    headlineContent = {
68	        Row(verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
69	            Text("Inbox")
70	            Spacer(Modifier.width(8.dp))
71	            Badge { Text("3") }
72	        }
73	    },
74	    onClick = { … },
75	)
76	```
77	
78	### Slot naming
79	
80	- Use `xxxContent` for free-form `@Composable () -> Unit` slots (`headlineContent`, `supportingContent`, `trailingContent`) — matches Material 3.
81	- Use a singular noun (`title`, `icon`, `actions`) when the slot is semantically constrained and the component name disambiguates (`Scaffold(topBar = { … }, bottomBar = { … }, floatingActionButton = { … })`).
82	- Don't use `content` *and* other `xxxContent` slots together — pick one convention per component.
83	
84	## 2. Scope receivers when the slot emits into a layout
85	
86	If the slot's content will sit inside a `Row`/`Column`/`Box` whose layout features (`Modifier.weight`, `BoxScope.matchParentSize`, alignment) should be available to the caller, declare the slot as a receiver lambda: `@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit`.
87	
88	```kotlin
89	// ❌ BAD — actions render inside a Row, but callers can't use RowScope.weight()
90	@Composable
91	fun MyTopBar(
92	    title: @Composable () -> Unit,
93	    actions: @Composable () -> Unit = {},   // ← caller has no Row scope
94	)
95	```
96	
97	```kotlin
98	// ✅ GOOD — caller gets RowScope; .weight() and alignment-by works inside
99	@Composable
100	fun MyTopBar(
101	    title: @Composable () -> Unit,
102	    actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit = {},
103	)
104	```
105	
106	This is what makes `TopAppBar(actions = { IconButton(…); IconButton(…) })` work — the caller is implicitly inside a `RowScope`.
107	
108	Don't bolt a scope receiver onto every slot reflexively. The receiver should match the actual parent layout the slot emits into. If the slot is rendered inside a `Box`, use `BoxScope`. If it's inside a `Column`, use `ColumnScope`. If the parent is not a standard layout (or none of its scope APIs are useful in slot content), no receiver.
109	
110	## 3. Optional slots — nullable with `null` default
111	
112	For slots that may be absent, prefer `(@Composable () -> Unit)? = null` over `@Composable () -> Unit = {}`:
113	
114	```kotlin
115	// ❌ BAD — empty default; "no leading content" is the empty lambda
116	leadingContent: @Composable () -> Unit = {}
117	
118	// ✅ GOOD — null means "no slot"; the component can omit space/padding when absent
119	leadingContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null
120	```
121	
122	With a nullable slot, the component can branch on `leadingContent != null` and skip the slot's container, spacing, and padding entirely. With an empty default, the layout often still allocates space for absent content.
123	
124	## 4. Defaults live in `XxxDefaults`
125	
126	When you find yourself documenting "the trailing slot should usually be a chevron" or "pass `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface` for the default background", co-locate the helpers in a `XxxDefaults` object next to the component:
127	
128	```kotlin
129	object SettingsRowDefaults {
130	    @Composable
131	    fun Chevron() = Icon(
132	        imageVector = Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.KeyboardArrowRight,
133	        contentDescription = null,
134	    )
135	
136	    @Composable
137	    fun TrailingValue(text: String) = Text(
138	        text = text,
139	        style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium,
140	        color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
141	    )
142	}
143	```
144	
145	Call sites stay declarative for the common cases and the slot is still fully open for one-offs:
146	
147	```kotlin
148	SettingsRow(
149	    headlineContent = { Text("Notifications") },
150	    trailingContent = { SettingsRowDefaults.Chevron() },
151	    onClick = { … },
152	)
153	```
154	
155	This matches Material 3's `ButtonDefaults`, `TopAppBarDefaults`, etc. — defaults that are themselves composable belong here, not as new component parameters with `MaterialTheme.x.y` defaults expanded inline.
156	
157	## Quick reference
158	
159	| Symptom | Diagnosis | Fix |
160	|---|---|---|
161	| `title: String, subtitle: String?, leadingIcon: ImageVector?` on a reusable component | Primitive content params (§1) | Convert to `xxxContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)?` slots |
162	| Multiple boolean flags (`showChevron`, `showSwitch`) selecting trailing shapes | Enumerating shapes (§1) | One `trailingContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)?` slot |
163	| A `mode: Mode.Sealed` parameter listing variants | Same as flag soup (§1) | Slot it |
164	| `actions: @Composable () -> Unit = {}` inside a `Row` body | Missing scope receiver (§2) | `actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit = {}` |
165	| `slot: @Composable () -> Unit = {}` for an optional area | Empty-lambda default (§3) | `slot: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null` and branch on it |
166	| Component param `defaultColor: Color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface` | Defaults inlined (§4) | Move to `XxxDefaults.color` and reference it |
167	| Common trailing content repeats at every call site | Missing default helper (§4) | Add `XxxDefaults.Chevron()` etc. |
168	
169	## When NOT to apply
170	
171	- **Single-use components.** A composable used in exactly one place, with no plan to reuse, doesn't benefit from slot flexibility — and the slot indirection makes the code harder to read for the one reader. Primitive params + inline content is fine. (As soon as a second call site appears, slot it.)
172	- **Design-system primitives where every caller must look identical.** A `Heading2(text: String)` exists *because* you want every H2 to look the same; making it `headlineContent: @Composable () -> Unit` invites callers to break the rule. Keep it primitive. (Conversely: if `Heading2` ever needs a badge inline, slot it.)
173	- **Semantic parameters the component intentionally owns.** If the component owns typography, iconography, accessibility wording, or product consistency, a primitive parameter may be the constraint you want.
174	- **Constrained-type parameters that genuinely are constrained.** A `Switch(checked: Boolean, onCheckedChange: ...)` doesn't need its checked indicator to be a slot. Booleans-with-callbacks are not "content."
175	- **Performance-critical fast paths** (rare in app code; common in framework primitives). A slot is an allocated lambda. In the deepest LazyList item layer, sometimes primitives win. If you're not writing the framework, this doesn't apply.
176	
177	## Red flags during review
178	
179	| Thought | Reality |
180	|---|---|
181	| "Title is *always* a String — making it a slot is over-engineering" | "Always today" is the trap. Material's `ListItem.headlineContent` exists because tomorrow someone wants a `Text + Badge`. The slot is `8` characters of extra wrapping at every call site (`{ Text(…) }`); the refactor to add a slot later edits every existing call site. |
182	| "Lambdas are heavier than strings" | At the scale of typical Compose UI, this isn't measurable — and the framework's own components (`Button`, `ListItem`, `TopAppBar`, `Scaffold`) all slot. If your component is in the hottest of hot paths, see "When NOT to apply." |
183	| "I'll add a slot later if someone asks" | The slot turns one parameter into two parameters (the slot itself + maybe an internal flag) and edits every call site. The shape change isn't a "later" change. |
184	| "I'll model the variants with a sealed `Trailing` type instead" | Sealed enumeration is bounded; slots are unbounded. A sealed type works *until* the day someone needs a variant you didn't anticipate — at which point you're back to editing the component. The slot avoids the cycle. |
185	| "The leading area is *always* an icon, the trailing area varies — I'll slot only the trailing" | This is the partial-slot trap. The "always-an-icon" assumption breaks the first time a row needs an avatar or a flag emoji or a coloured shape. Slot leading too. |
186	| "There's only one call site today" | If there's only one call site, you're probably not designing a reusable component yet. See "When NOT to apply" — primitives are fine for a true single-use. The moment you copy-paste it, slot it. |
187	
188	## Related
189	
190	- [`compose-modifier-and-layout-style`](../compose-modifier-and-layout-style/SKILL.md) — the modifier-parameter rule (§1–§3 there) travels with slot APIs. A reusable component takes a `modifier` parameter *and* slots its content; the caller owns both placement and what to place.

1	# Compose View Composition — slot-authoring rules
2	
3	**The slot pattern and the `modifier` parameter form one paired API contract:** the caller owns *what to place* (slots) and *placement* (modifier). This file covers the slot side; see `compose/references/modifiers.md` for the modifier authoring rules.
4	
5	This reference covers how to author a slot API correctly — the six rules below.
6	
7	## Slot authoring rules
8	
9	### 1. Carry the parent's receiver scope on the slot — don't silently drop it
10	
11	When a slot renders inside a standard layout (`Row`, `Column`, `Box`, `LazyListScope`) whose scope exposes useful caller-facing APIs, the slot type **must** carry that receiver: a slot rendered inside a `Row` is `@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit`, inside a `Box` is `@Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit`. Writing it as a bare `@Composable () -> Unit` instead is a **silent API regression** — it strips `RowScope.weight()`, `ColumnScope.weight()`, `BoxScope.matchParentSize()`, and `BoxScope.align()` from every caller, and nothing flags it because the code still compiles.
12	
13	**Don't reflexively scope every slot** — only when the parent's scope offers something the caller meaningfully needs. A slot rendered inside a custom `Layout {}` with no public scope shouldn't be scoped just for symmetry (leaking an internal scope is its own smell).
14	
15	```kotlin
16	// ✅ RIGHT — actions land in a Row; the receiver lets callers .weight() and .align()
17	@Composable
18	fun TopAppBar(
19	    title: @Composable () -> Unit,
20	    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
21	    actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit = {},   // scoped: caller gets .weight() / .align()
22	) {
23	    Row(modifier = modifier) {
24	        title()
25	        Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f))
26	        actions()
27	    }
28	}
29	
30	// ❌ WRONG — bare lambda silently strips RowScope from every caller
31	fun TopAppBar(/* … */ actions: @Composable () -> Unit = {})
32	
33	// ❌ ALSO WRONG — scoping a custom Layout's internal scope the caller has no use for
34	fun MyCustomLayout(content: @Composable MyInternalScope.() -> Unit)
35	```
36	
37	### 2. Optional slots: nullable, not empty-lambda
38	
39	**DO** use `slot: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null` for optional slots and branch on `null` to omit the surrounding spacing/padding/divider. **DON'T** use `slot: @Composable () -> Unit = {}`.
40	
41	**WHY:** an empty lambda is still *invoked* — it emits nothing, but the parent layout can't tell, so any `Spacer`, padding, divider, or container allocated for that slot stays in the layout, producing ghost space. With `null`, the component branches and omits the surrounding layout machinery entirely.
42	
43	```kotlin
44	// ❌ WRONG — empty default leaves ghost space
45	@Composable
46	fun ListItem(
47	    title: @Composable () -> Unit,
48	    trailing: @Composable () -> Unit = {},          // ❌ empty lambda
49	) {
50	    Row {
51	        title()
52	        Spacer(Modifier.width(8.dp))                // ❌ unconditional — nothing signals it to be omitted
53	        trailing()                                  // emits nothing, but the Spacer already added 8.dp
54	    }
55	}
56	
57	// ✅ RIGHT — nullable lets the component omit the spacer
58	@Composable
59	fun ListItem(
60	    title: @Composable () -> Unit,
61	    trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
62	) {
63	    Row {
64	        title()
65	        if (trailing != null) {
66	            Spacer(Modifier.width(8.dp))
67	            trailing()
68	        }
69	    }
70	}
71	```
72	
73	### 3. `XxxDefaults` object for composable defaults
74	
75	When a slot has a sensible default that is itself a composable, expose it via a public `XxxDefaults` object — not as an inline default expression on the parameter.
76	
77	**WHY:** composable default expressions (`trailingContent: @Composable () -> Unit = { Icon(...) }`) hide the default in the signature, can't be reused by callers who want "the default plus one more thing," and tangle the default's implementation with the API surface. A `XxxDefaults` object mirrors Material 3 (`ButtonDefaults`, `CardDefaults`, `TopAppBarDefaults`), is discoverable via autocomplete, and lets callers compose with the default explicitly.
78	
79	```kotlin
80	// ✅ RIGHT
81	@Composable
82	fun SettingsRow(
83	    title: String,
84	    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
85	    trailingContent: @Composable () -> Unit = SettingsRowDefaults.Chevron(),
86	) {
87	    Row(modifier = modifier) {
88	        Text(title, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f))
89	        trailingContent()
90	    }
91	}
92	
93	object SettingsRowDefaults {
94	    @Composable
95	    fun Chevron() = Icon(Icons.AutoMirrored.Default.KeyboardArrowRight, contentDescription = null)
96	}
97	
98	SettingsRow(title = "Notifications")                            // default chevron
99	SettingsRow(title = "Logout", trailingContent = {})            // suppress
100	SettingsRow(title = "Theme", trailingContent = { Switch(...) }) // custom
101	```
102	
103	### 4. Naming convention
104	
105	| Slot shape | Naming | Examples |
106	|------------|--------|----------|
107	| Free-form, multi-element | `xxxContent` or bare `content` | M3's `content`, `bottomBar`, `floatingActionButton`, `topBar` |
108	| Semantically constrained, singular role | Singular noun | `title`, `actions`, `icon`, `label`, `trailing` |
109	
110	**WHY:** Material 3 already established this vocabulary (`Scaffold(content = …)`, `TopAppBar(title = …)`, `ListItem(trailingContent = …)`). Matching it makes your APIs feel native; deviating creates friction. **Don't mix bare `content` with other `xxxContent` slots in one component** — either every free-form slot is `xxxContent`, or your single main slot is bare `content`, not both.
111	
112	### 5. Boolean-flag / sealed-variant smells
113	
114	When you reach for `showChevron: Boolean`, `mode: TrailingMode`, or "I'll model trailing variants with a sealed `Trailing` type" — **that's a slot trying to be born.** Replace it with `xxxContent: @Composable () -> Unit`.
115	
116	**WHY:** boolean flags and sealed variants enumerate the cases *you* thought of; a slot lets the caller decide. Every new variant becomes a caller-side composable, not an API change.
117	
118	```kotlin
119	// ❌ WRONG — boolean enumerates one of N future cases (what about a switch? a badge? a count?)
120	fun SettingsRow(title: String, showChevron: Boolean = true)
121	
122	// ❌ WRONG — sealed variant is just a worse slot; every new case touches the API
123	sealed interface Trailing { /* Chevron, None, Switch(...), Badge(count) … */ }
124	fun SettingsRow(title: String, trailing: Trailing = Trailing.Chevron)
125	
126	// ✅ RIGHT — slot; callers compose any variant freely, no API change
127	@Composable
128	fun SettingsRow(
129	    title: String,
130	    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
131	    trailingContent: @Composable () -> Unit = SettingsRowDefaults.Chevron(),
132	) { /* … */ }
133	
134	SettingsRow("Wi-Fi", trailingContent = { Switch(checked = on, onCheckedChange = {}) })
135	SettingsRow("Inbox", trailingContent = { Badge { Text("99+") } })
136	```
137	
138	### 6. Partial-slot trap
139	
140	If you slot the trailing area but keep `leadingIcon: ImageVector` because "leading is always an icon," you've left the API half-rigid for no real reason. **Slot all the variable areas, or none.**
141	
142	**WHY:** "leading is always an icon" is a load-bearing assumption that fails the first time someone needs a `CircularProgressIndicator`, an `Image`, an avatar, or an icon-with-badge there. A `@Composable () -> Unit` slot costs nothing extra at the common call site (still `{ Icon(...) }`) and absorbs every future variant for free.
143	
144	```kotlin
145	// ❌ WRONG — partial-slot: trailing is flexible, leading is hardcoded to an icon
146	@Composable
147	fun ListItem(title: String, leadingIcon: ImageVector, trailingContent: @Composable () -> Unit = {}) { /* … */ }
148	
149	// ✅ RIGHT — both flexible areas are slots
150	@Composable
151	fun ListItem(
152	    title: String,
153	    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
154	    leadingContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
155	    trailingContent: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
156	) {
157	    Row(modifier = modifier) {
158	        leadingContent?.invoke()
159	        Text(title, Modifier.weight(1f))
160	        trailingContent?.invoke()
161	    }
162	}
163	
164	ListItem(title = "Profile", leadingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.Person, null) })            // common case, cheap
165	ListItem(title = "Syncing", leadingContent = { CircularProgressIndicator(Modifier.size(20.dp)) }) // complex, no API change
166	```

5	
6	# Compose modifier and layout style
7	
8	## Core principle
9	
10	A composable that emits layout is a leaf the *parent* places — the parent decides position, size, alignment, padding. The composable's job is structure (what's inside), not placement (where it goes). Three rules follow:
11	
12	- **Declare a `modifier` parameter and apply it to the root**, so the parent can actually do its job. Hardcoding `.fillMaxWidth()` on a composable's root takes that decision away from every future caller.
13	- **Construct modifier chains as one fluent expression**, not stepwise reassignments. Both compile to the same thing, but the chain *reads* as intent in one pass.
14	- **Conditional rendering belongs where the condition applies.** A layout call whose only content is one `if` exists solely to hold the condition — push the `if` outside instead.
15	
16	These travel together because the same composable usually triggers all three: you declare its parameters (rule 1), the caller constructs a chain to position it (rules 2), and the body has a conditional you might be tempted to wrap (rule 3).
17	
18	## When to use this skill
19	
20	- You're writing a `@Composable fun` that calls a layout (`Box`, `Column`, `Row`, `LazyColumn`, `Text`, `Image`, `Surface`, `Card`, `Layout { … }`, anything from `compose.foundation.layout` or `compose.material*`) and its signature has no `modifier` parameter, or has one that isn't applied to the root, or has a hardcoded `.fillMaxWidth()`/`.padding(...)` on the root.
21	- You see `var m = Modifier` followed by `m = m.padding(…)`, `m = m.background(…)`, etc.
22	- A `modifier = …` argument has three or more chained calls on a single line.
23	- A composable's body is `Layout { if (cond) Content() }` — one conditional, nothing else.
24	
25	## 1. Declare a `modifier` parameter
26	
27	For composables that emit layout, prefer a `modifier` parameter after required parameters and before content/lambda parameters, with a default of `Modifier`. The name is exactly `modifier` — not `mod`, not `m`, not `wrapperModifier`.
28	
29	```kotlin
30	// ❌ BAD — no modifier param; caller can't position, size, or constrain this
31	@Composable
32	fun HomeScreenHeader(title: String, subtitle: String) {
33	    Column(
34	        modifier = Modifier
35	            .fillMaxWidth()
36	            .padding(horizontal = 16.dp),
37	        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(4.dp),
38	    ) {
39	        Text(title, style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineLarge)
40	        Text(subtitle, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium)
41	    }
42	}
43	```
44	
45	```kotlin
46	// ✅ GOOD — parent decides width and padding; the composable describes structure only
47	@Composable
48	fun HomeScreenHeader(
49	    title: String,
50	    subtitle: String,
51	    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
52	) {
53	    Column(
54	        modifier = modifier,
55	        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(4.dp),
56	    ) {
57	        Text(title, style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineLarge)
58	        Text(subtitle, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium)
59	    }
60	}
61	```
62	
63	The caller now writes `HomeScreenHeader(title, subtitle, Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(horizontal = 16.dp))` once, at the home screen — the only place that knows the layout actually wants those.
64	
65	## 2. Apply the caller's modifier to the root, and apply it first
66	
67	When the root layout already takes other arguments (alignment, arrangement, padding *that's intrinsic to the composable*), the caller-provided modifier still goes on the root layout's `modifier` parameter — and the composable's local chain is appended after.
68	
69	```kotlin
70	// ❌ BAD — modifier accepted but never applied
71	@Composable
72	fun Avatar(url: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
73	    Image(painter = rememberAsyncImagePainter(url), contentDescription = null)
74	}
75	
76	// ❌ BAD — applied to a child, not the root; caller's size/position changes don't take
77	@Composable
78	fun Avatar(url: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
79	    Box {
80	        Image(
81	            painter = rememberAsyncImagePainter(url),
82	            contentDescription = null,
83	            modifier = modifier,
84	        )
85	    }
86	}
87	
88	// ❌ BAD — caller's modifier ends up last, so the composable's own size wins
89	@Composable
90	fun Avatar(url: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
91	    Image(
92	        painter = rememberAsyncImagePainter(url),
93	        contentDescription = null,
94	        modifier = Modifier
95	            .clip(CircleShape)
96	            .size(48.dp)
97	            .then(modifier),
98	    )
99	}
100	```
101	
102	```kotlin
103	// ✅ GOOD — caller's modifier first, then the composable's intrinsic chain
104	@Composable
105	fun Avatar(url: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
106	    Image(
107	        painter = rememberAsyncImagePainter(url),
108	        contentDescription = null,
109	        modifier = modifier
110	            .clip(CircleShape)
111	            .size(48.dp),
112	    )
113	}
114	```
115	
116	Order matters: in a modifier chain, the *earlier* segment is the outer wrapper. The caller's modifier should be the outermost so caller-provided `.size(...)` or `.padding(...)` can override the composable's defaults rather than being overridden by them.
117	
118	## 3. Don't hardcode layout decisions on the root
119	
120	If the composable's root has `.fillMaxWidth()`, `.padding(horizontal = 16.dp)`, `.height(56.dp)`, etc., the caller can't *not* have them. Those are layout choices the parent should own.
121	
122	```kotlin
123	// ❌ BAD — every caller now fills max width whether they want to or not
124	@Composable
125	fun PrimaryButton(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
126	    Button(
127	        onClick = onClick,
128	        modifier = modifier.fillMaxWidth(),   // ← hardcoded
129	    ) { Text(text) }
130	}
131	
132	// ✅ GOOD — caller adds .fillMaxWidth() if (and only if) they want it
133	@Composable
134	fun PrimaryButton(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
135	    Button(onClick = onClick, modifier = modifier) { Text(text) }
136	}
137	```
138	
139	The carve-out is for modifiers that are part of the **identity** of the composable — what makes an `Avatar` an avatar (the `.clip(CircleShape)` and a default `.size(48.dp)`), not where it sits on the screen. Test: can you imagine a caller wanting a version of this composable *without* that modifier? If yes, push it out. If no (an avatar without `clip(CircleShape)` isn't an avatar), keep it — but put it *after* the caller's modifier in the chain (see §2).
140	
141	## 4. Construct modifier chains as one fluent expression
142	
143	Recomposition re-runs the composable body — every modifier expression is re-evaluated. Reassigning `var modifier =` step-by-step looks plausible but breaks the visual flow, invites further mutation, and produces nothing a chain doesn't.
144	
145	```kotlin
146	// ❌ BAD — visual flow broken into reassignments; `var` invites more mutation
147	@Composable
148	fun Demo() {
149	    var m = Modifier
150	    m = m.padding(16.dp)
151	    m = m.fillMaxSize()
152	    Box(m) { }
153	}
154	
155	// ❌ ALSO BAD — same shape, dressed up with .then()
156	@Composable
157	fun Demo() {
158	    var m = Modifier
159	    m = m.padding(16.dp)
160	    m = m.then(Modifier.fillMaxSize())
161	    Box(m) { }
162	}
163	```
164	
165	```kotlin
166	// ✅ GOOD
167	@Composable
168	fun Demo() {
169	    val m = Modifier
170	        .padding(16.dp)
171	        .fillMaxSize()
172	    Box(m) { }
173	}
174	```
175	
176	`val`, not `var`: once the chain is built, nothing should re-bind it. The reassignment shape is what makes `var` look necessary; the chain shape doesn't need it.
177	
178	### Inline at the call site is fine for short chains
179	
180	For one or two calls, build the modifier inline. The "extract to a `val`" rule only earns its keep when the chain is long enough to be worth naming, or when the same chain repeats.
181	
182	```kotlin
183	// ✅ GOOD — short chain inline
184	Box(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) { … }
185	Box(modifier = Modifier.padding(8.dp).background(Color.Red)) { … }
186	```
187	
188	### Conditional segments stay on the chain
189	
190	A common reason to reach for `var` is "the modifier depends on a condition." It doesn't — splice the condition inline:
191	
192	```kotlin
193	// ✅ GOOD — conditional inside the chain, still one expression
194	Box(
195	    modifier = Modifier
196	        .fillMaxWidth()
197	        .then(if (selected) Modifier.background(Color.Red) else Modifier),
198	)
199	```
200	
201	`Modifier` (the empty modifier) is the identity element for `.then` — it lets you keep the chain shape when one branch contributes nothing.
202	
203	## 5. Multiline formatting at the call site
204	
205	When a `modifier` argument's chain has **three or more** calls, format multiline with one call per line. Indent the chain so the dotted calls align beneath the value.
206	
207	```kotlin
208	// ❌ BAD — three+ calls on one line; hard to scan
209	Box(
210	    modifier = modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(16.dp).weight(1f),
211	)
212	
213	// ✅ GOOD
214	Box(
215	    modifier = modifier
216	        .fillMaxSize()
217	        .padding(16.dp)
218	        .weight(1f),
219	)
220	```
221	
222	One or two calls stay on a single line — the threshold is the call count, not the character count. If a single call has very long arguments, that's a different problem (extract a `val`, or shorten the arguments).
223	
224	This applies *only* to a parameter named `modifier`. Other fluent-style arguments aren't covered here.
225	
226	## 6. Hoist single conditionals out of the layout
227	
228	When a layout's *only* content is one `if`, the layout exists solely to "hold" the conditional. Move the `if` outside — the layout will only exist when it has something to show.
229	
230	```kotlin
231	// ❌ BAD — Column always emitted; only its inner content is conditional
232	@Composable
233	fun A() {
234	    Column {
235	        if (showHeader) {
236	            Text("Title")
237	            Text("Subtitle")
238	        }
239	    }
240	}
241	
242	// ✅ GOOD — Column only exists when it has content
243	@Composable
244	fun A() {
245	    if (showHeader) {
246	        Column {
247	            Text("Title")
248	            Text("Subtitle")
249	        }
250	    }
251	}
252	```
253	
254	The benefit isn't a performance win — the runtime handles both fine — it's that the second form *reads* as "header section, conditionally." The first reads as "always-on column that may or may not have content."
255	
256	### The carve-outs (and why)
257	
258	- **Layout carries visual semantics that aren't conditional.** When the layout call passes `modifier`, `contentAlignment`, `horizontalArrangement`, or `verticalAlignment`, those arguments describe the *container*, not the content. Hoisting the conditional either loses those (the container collapses with the content) or duplicates them into both branches. Leave it.
259	
260	  ```kotlin
261	  // ✅ KEEP AS-IS — modifier on the container is doing visible work
262	  @Composable
263	  fun A(modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
264	      Box(modifier = modifier) {
265	          if (something) {
266	              Text("Bleh1")
267	              Text("Bleh2")
268	          }
269	      }
270	  }
271	  ```
272	
273	- **There are siblings to the `if`.** The layout has other content; the `if` is just one piece. Hoisting either pulls the siblings out (changing the layout) or leaves a different shape behind. Leave it.
274	
275	- **`if … else …` with both branches contributing composables.** Both branches do work; nothing to hoist; the layout *is* the shared container.
276	
277	  ```kotlin
278	  // ✅ KEEP AS-IS — both branches contribute to the layout
279	  Box {
280	      if (something) Text("Hint") else innerTextField()
281	  }
282	  ```
283	
284	## 7. Measure-phase constraint decoration
285	
286	When composable A captures a size and composable B must match it, **do not read the captured size in B's composable body** (`Modifier.height(state.dp)`). That ties B to composition whenever the measurement state changes.
287	
288	Capture in a layout callback on A; apply on B inside `Modifier.layout` so only layout invalidates:
289	
290	```kotlin
291	fun Modifier.decorateMeasureConstraints(
292	    decorate: (Constraints) -> Constraints,
293	): Modifier = layout { measurable, incoming ->
294	    val constraints = decorate(incoming).constrain(incoming)
295	    val placeable = measurable.measure(constraints)
296	    layout(placeable.width, placeable.height) {
297	        placeable.placeRelative(0, 0)
298	    }
299	}
300	```
301	
302	```kotlin
303	// Hoisted at the common parent of both rows:
304	//   var anchorHeightPx by remember { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
305	
306	// Measured row — write state only from onSizeChanged
307	RowAnchor(Modifier.onSizeChanged { size -> if (size.height != anchorHeightPx) anchorHeightPx = size.height })
308	
309	// Sibling rows — read anchorHeightPx only inside layout
310	RowSibling(
311	    Modifier.decorateMeasureConstraints { incoming ->
312	        if (anchorHeightPx > 0) {
313	            // Clamp to incoming bounds so the constraint never exceeds the parent's max.
314	            incoming.copy(minHeight = anchorHeightPx, maxHeight = anchorHeightPx)
315	        } else {
316	            incoming
317	        }
318	    },
319	)
320	```
321	
322	Use a composition-time fallback (fixed height) only while `anchorHeightPx` is `0`. See [`compose-state-deferred-reads`](../compose-state-deferred-reads/SKILL.md) for the full cross-row pattern.
323	
324	## Quick reference
325	
326	| Symptom | Diagnosis | Fix |
327	|---|---|---|
328	| `@Composable fun Foo(text: String)` with `Column`/`Box`/`Text` in body | No `modifier` param (§1) | Add `modifier: Modifier = Modifier`; pass to root |
329	| `modifier: Modifier = Modifier` declared but never referenced | Param ignored (§2) | Apply to root layout's `modifier` arg |
330	| `modifier` passed to a child, not the root | Wrong target (§2) | Move to the outermost layout's `modifier` |
331	| `modifier = Modifier.x().y().then(modifier)` | Caller's modifier last (§2) | Reorder: `modifier = modifier.x().y()` |
332	| `modifier = modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(...)` on a general-purpose component | Layout hardcoded (§3) | Remove the hardcoded calls; let callers add them |
333	| Sibling composables in the file don't have `modifier` either | Spreading anti-pattern | Fix this one; fix siblings opportunistically |
334	| `mod: Modifier = Modifier` or `wrapperModifier: Modifier = Modifier` | Wrong name (§1) | Rename to exactly `modifier` |
335	| `var m = Modifier` followed by `m = m.xxx()` reassignments | Stepwise modifier construction (§4) | One fluent chain on a `val`, or build inline |
336	| `var m = Modifier; m = m.then(Modifier.xxx())` | Same shape via `.then` (§4) | Collapse `.then(Modifier.x())` to `.x()` in the chain |
337	| Modifier branch needs a condition | Reaching for `var` (§4) | `.then(if (c) Modifier.x() else Modifier)` inside the chain |
338	| `modifier = modifier.a().b().c()` on one line | Long chain not formatted (§5) | One call per line, indented under the value |
339	| `Layout { if (cond) X() }` with no other content and no layout-tuning args | Hoist (§6) | Move the `if` outside the layout |
340	| `Box(modifier = …) { if (cond) X() }` | Layout carries semantics — leave (§6 carve-out) | Keep as-is |
341	| `Box { if (cond) X() else Y() }` | Both branches contribute — leave (§6 carve-out) | Keep as-is |
342	| Sibling lazy row reads `height(state)` from another row's measurement | Composition-time size coupling (§7) | Capture on measured row; apply via `decorateMeasureConstraints` on siblings |
343	
344	## When NOT to apply
345	
346	- **Composables that don't emit layout.** A `@Composable fun computeColor(): Color` or a `@Composable @ReadOnlyComposable` accessor doesn't emit a layout node. No `modifier` parameter needed (and a `@ReadOnlyComposable` couldn't accept one — see `compose-state-authoring`).
347	- **`@Preview` functions.** Previews are throwaway entry points; the framework calls them with no caller. A `modifier` parameter would be unused dead weight.
348	- **Test-only composables** inside `*Test` sources whose only caller is `composeTestRule.setContent { … }`. Same reasoning as previews.
349	- **Internal layout primitives that take a `modifier` as their *first required* parameter** (very rare; framework-level). The rule is "first *optional* param"; some private utilities legitimately have `modifier` upfront as required.
350	- **Modifier assembled imperatively from animation state.** A modifier built by appending values from `Animatable` or other procedural sources may legitimately need intermediate variables. The chain isn't the goal; readability is. If the chain becomes a worse expression, write the imperative form.
351	- **Slot APIs that store modifiers** in a data class or builder (rare; usually framework-level code). The fluent-chain idea is about user-site construction.
352	- **Test composables** pinning specific recomposition shapes — usually fine either way; don't refactor test composables purely for style.
353	
354	The declaration-side rules (§1–§3) should not be skipped merely because "this composable is internal", "only used in one place", "I'd rather not have the extra parameter on the signature", or "we know all the callers already". Those are exactly the rationalisations that produce composables that become single-use the day someone wants to call them twice.
355	
356	## Red flags during review
357	
358	| Thought | Reality |
359	|---|---|
360	| "This composable is internal-only — adding `modifier` is over-engineering" | The parameter is eight characters and a default. It's not over-engineering; it's the convention. Skipping it is the over-engineering — it's a custom decision against the grain of every Compose API. |
361	| "It's only used in one place, so I know the layout requirements" | "Only used in one place" describes today. The cost of the parameter is paid once; the cost of refactoring callers when the second use site appears is paid per caller. |
362	| "The sibling composables in this file don't have `modifier` either, so I'm matching style" | Spreading an anti-pattern isn't matching style. Fix this one. Fix the siblings opportunistically. |
363	| "The parent always wants `.fillMaxWidth()` here" | Then the parent passes `.fillMaxWidth()`. The composable doesn't decide that for callers it hasn't met yet. |
364	| "I'll add it when someone needs it" | You're someone. You need it now (for the convention). The next caller won't add it either — they'll work around its absence. |
365	| "It's a tiny composable — the modifier param is noise" | The param is eight characters at the declaration and zero characters at any call site that doesn't need it. The "noise" is imagined. |
366	| "I added `modifier` but kept `.fillMaxWidth()` on the root so the home screen doesn't have to" | Then the *not*-home-screen caller can't unset it. Move the `.fillMaxWidth()` to the caller. |
367	| "I need `var` for the modifier because the chain depends on a condition" | A conditional segment is `.then(if (c) Modifier.x() else Modifier)`, still on one chain. No `var` needed. |
368	| "Three lines is too few to make multiline" | Three chained calls *is* the threshold. Below three, one line. At or above three, multiline. |
369	| "The Column adds nothing but I'll keep it for symmetry" | Then hoist the conditional and keep the Column inside the consequent — symmetry preserved, no always-on container. |
370	| "I'll put the `if` inside because the layout already exists" | "Already exists" is the bug. The layout shouldn't exist when the condition is false. |

1	# Jetpack Compose Modifiers Reference
2	
3	> **Modifier and slots together form the public-API contract of any reusable composable.** The caller owns *placement* (the `modifier` parameter) and *what to place* (the content slots). This file covers the modifier side; see `compose/references/view-composition.md` for the slot authoring rules.
4	
5	This reference covers the **API-contract rules** for the modifier parameter, plus the chain-ordering reference other files point here for — not the modifier catalogue itself.
6	
7	## Modifier as API Contract
8	
9	Every reusable composable has a public surface: a `modifier` parameter and (often) content slots. The rules below govern the modifier half of that contract. Violating them silently breaks callers — sizes won't apply, paddings stack twice, and the composable becomes un-reusable outside its original screen.
10	
11	### Rule 1 — Param naming is exact
12	
13	Any composable that emits layout MUST declare `modifier: Modifier = Modifier`. The name must be literally `modifier` — not `mod`, `m`, `wrapperModifier`, or `outerModifier`. Place it after required params and before content lambdas.
14	
15	```kotlin
16	// WRONG — non-standard names break tooling, lint, and reader expectations
17	@Composable
18	fun Avatar(url: String, m: Modifier = Modifier) { ... }
19	
20	@Composable
21	fun Card(wrapperModifier: Modifier = Modifier, content: @Composable () -> Unit) { ... }
22	
23	// RIGHT — canonical signature: required params, modifier with default, then slots
24	@Composable
25	fun Avatar(url: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) { ... }
26	
27	@Composable
28	fun Card(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, content: @Composable () -> Unit) { ... }
29	```
30	
31	**Why:** Lint rules (`ComposableModifierParameterPosition`, `ModifierParameter`), Android Studio's inspections, and every Compose codebase convention assume this exact name and position. Renaming it breaks IDE auto-import of `Modifier.Companion`, defeats lint, and surprises every reader. The default value `= Modifier` lets callers omit it; the name `modifier` is non-negotiable.
32	
33	### Rule 2 — Apply the caller's modifier to the ROOT layout, not a child
34	
35	Caller-supplied modifiers like `.size(...)`, `.padding(...)`, or `.weight(...)` must reach the outermost emitted node.
36	
37	```kotlin
38	// WRONG — caller's .size(120.dp) lands on the inner Image, not the outer Box.
39	// The Box still measures intrinsic, so the Avatar is the wrong size in its parent's layout.
40	@Composable
41	fun Avatar(url: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
42	    Box {
43	        Image(
44	            painter = rememberAsyncImagePainter(url),
45	            contentDescription = null,
46	            modifier = modifier  // wrong node
47	        )
48	    }
49	}
50	
51	// RIGHT — modifier reaches the outermost node; child layout stays internal
52	@Composable
53	fun Avatar(url: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
54	    Box(modifier = modifier) {
55	        Image(
56	            painter = rememberAsyncImagePainter(url),
57	            contentDescription = null
58	        )
59	    }
60	}
61	```
62	
63	**Why:** Layout modifiers measure the node they're attached to. If the caller writes `Avatar(modifier = Modifier.size(120.dp))`, they expect the *Avatar* — the unit the parent positions — to be 120dp. Routing the modifier to a child silently drops sizing/weight/padding constraints from the parent's perspective and produces hard-to-debug layout bugs.
64	
65	### Rule 3 — Caller's modifier comes FIRST in the chain
66	
67	Caller modifiers must precede internal modifiers so the caller's intent wins. The only exception: modifiers tied to the composable's visual *identity* (e.g., `Avatar`'s `.clip(CircleShape)`) may follow.
68	
69	```kotlin
70	// WRONG — hardcoded chain first; caller's modifier overridden
71	@Composable
72	fun Avatar(modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
73	    Box(modifier = Modifier.size(48.dp).clip(CircleShape).then(modifier)) { ... }
74	}
75	
76	// RIGHT — caller's modifier first; identity modifier (clip) after
77	@Composable
78	fun Avatar(modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
79	    Box(modifier = modifier.clip(CircleShape)) { ... }
80	}
81	```
82	
83	**Why:** Whichever `.size(...)` appears first wins for the outer measurement the parent sees. Putting a hardcoded `.size(48.dp)` first makes a caller's `.size(120.dp)` a no-op for the Avatar's outer dimensions. Caller intent must come first; only modifiers that define what the composable *is* (a circular crop for `Avatar`) belong after.
84	
85	### Rule 4 — No hardcoded placement on a reusable root
86	
87	A reusable composable's root MUST NOT carry `.fillMaxWidth()`, `.height(56.dp)`, `.padding(horizontal = 16.dp)`, or any other placement decision. Placement is the parent's job — that's what the `modifier` parameter is for. (This is the one most often gotten wrong.)
88	
89	```kotlin
90	// WRONG — root hardcodes "I take full width and 56dp tall with horizontal padding".
91	// Caller cannot place this in a Row, give it a different size, or remove the padding.
92	@Composable
93	fun ListItem(text: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
94	    Row(
95	        modifier = modifier
96	            .fillMaxWidth()
97	            .height(56.dp)
98	            .padding(horizontal = 16.dp)
99	    ) {
100	        Text(text)
101	    }
102	}
103	
104	// RIGHT — placement is the caller's call; component only decides its own internals
105	@Composable
106	fun ListItem(text: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
107	    Row(modifier = modifier) {
108	        Text(text, modifier = Modifier.padding(horizontal = 16.dp))
109	    }
110	}
111	// Caller decides placement:
112	// ListItem("Hello", modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(56.dp))
113	```
114	
115	**Identity carve-out:** Visual-identity modifiers — the ones without which the composable wouldn't *be* that composable — may stay on the root. `.clip(CircleShape)` on `Avatar` qualifies. Apply them AFTER the caller's modifier in the chain (see Rule 3).
116	
117	**Why:** Hardcoded placement makes a composable usable only in the one screen it was extracted from. The moment another screen needs it at a different width, inside a `Row`, or without that padding, the only options are forking or wrapping. The `modifier` parameter exists precisely to let parents make these calls.
118	
119	### Rule 5 — No `var m = Modifier; m = m.x()` reassignment
120	
121	Modifier chains MUST be built as one fluent `val` expression. Conditional segments stay inline via `.then(if (cond) Modifier.x() else Modifier)`.
122	
123	```kotlin
124	// WRONG — imperative reassignment defeats the fluent design and hides the chain shape
125	@Composable
126	fun Banner(isError: Boolean, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
127	    var m = modifier
128	    m = m.fillMaxWidth()
129	    if (isError) m = m.background(Color.Red)
130	    m = m.padding(16.dp)
131	    Box(modifier = m) { ... }
132	}
133	
134	// RIGHT — one fluent val; conditional segment inlined with .then
135	@Composable
136	fun Banner(isError: Boolean, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
137	    Box(
138	        modifier = modifier
139	            .fillMaxWidth()
140	            .then(if (isError) Modifier.background(Color.Red) else Modifier)
141	            .padding(16.dp)
142	    ) { ... }
143	}
144	```
145	
146	**Why:** `Modifier` is an immutable, ordered chain — reassignment forces readers to mentally replay each statement to recover the final order, and scatters the chain across lines that look like state mutations. A single `val` makes the order explicit and the diff small. The `.then(...)` idiom is the supported pattern for conditionals.
147	
148	### Rule 6 — Multiline chain threshold: at least 3 calls
149	
150	Format the chain inline for 1–2 calls; multiline for 3 or more. (Applies only to parameters literally named `modifier`.)
151	
152	```kotlin
153	// 1–2 calls — inline
154	Box(modifier = modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(16.dp))
155	
156	// 3+ calls — multiline, each call on its own line
157	Box(
158	    modifier = modifier
159	        .fillMaxWidth()
160	        .padding(16.dp)
161	        .background(Color.Blue)
162	        .clip(RoundedCornerShape(8.dp))
163	)
164	```
165	
166	**Why:** Modifier order is load-bearing. Once a chain has three or more calls, ordering bugs become invisible in a one-liner, and diffs that add/remove a modifier touch the whole line. Multiline lets each modifier own a line and makes reorderings obvious in review (the AndroidX convention).
167	
168	### Rule 7 — Hoist a single `if` out of a layout
169	
170	When a layout composable's *only* content is one `if`, hoist the `if` to wrap the layout instead.
171	
172	```kotlin
173	// WRONG — the Box exists only to host an if; the Box itself is dead weight
174	@Composable
175	fun Screen(showBanner: Boolean) {
176	    Box {
177	        if (showBanner) Banner()
178	    }
179	}
180	
181	// RIGHT — hoist the if; no wasted layout node
182	@Composable
183	fun Screen(showBanner: Boolean) {
184	    if (showBanner) Banner()
185	}
186	```
187	
188	**Keep the wrapping layout when:** (a) it carries real semantics (a modifier, alignment, or arrangement doing work); (b) the `if` has siblings sharing the layout; or (c) it's an `if/else` where both branches need the same wrapper. **Why:** every layout composable creates a real layout node (measure + placement + recomposition scope); `Box { if (cond) Foo() }` allocates that node every recomposition just to sometimes show one child. See `compose/references/performance.md` for the cost model.
189	
190	## Modifier Chain Ordering
191	
192	Modifiers apply left-to-right in the DSL but conceptually wrap bottom-to-top — each wraps the content below it. **Order outer (layout/sizing) → inner (styling/interaction).**
193	
194	```kotlin
195	Modifier.background(Color.Red).padding(16.dp).size(100.dp)   // red wraps the padded 100dp box
196	Modifier.size(100.dp).padding(16.dp).background(Color.Red)   // 100dp box is padded, then the 132dp total gets red
197	```
198	
199	`.size` after `.padding` excludes the padding from the final outer size; `.clip` before `.background` clips the background to the shape (after, it doesn't). This is the ordering reference `compose/references/design-to-compose.md` and `view-composition.md` point here for.
200	
201	## Custom modifiers, semantics, testTag — defer
202	
203	- **Custom modifiers:** prefer the `Modifier.Node` / `ModifierNodeElement` API over the deprecated `composed { }` (which creates a composition scope per use and captures composition locals). The deprecation + migration path lives in `compose/references/deprecated-patterns.md`.
204	- **Semantics** (`contentDescription`, `role`, `clearAndSetSemantics`, `mergeDescendants`) and **`testTag`** are standard. For the more advanced a11y bits (traversal order via `traversalIndex`/`isTraversalGroup`, live-region mode) see `compose/references/accessibility.md`; for test-selector strategy (semantics-first over `testTag`) see `android-skills:android-testing`.

7	## 1. remember {} Without Configuration-Derived Key
8	
9	### Root Cause
10	
11	`remember {}` without keys caches the initial computation and never recalculates. When the remembered value derives from configuration state (screen dimensions, font scale, density), a configuration change (rotation, foldable posture, window resize) leaves the cached value stale.
12	
13	### Crash Pattern
14	
15	```kotlin
16	// BAD: shimmerCount is cached from initial screenHeightDp, stale after rotation
17	@Composable
18	fun ShimmerList() {
19	    val config = LocalConfiguration.current
20	    val screenHeightDp = config.screenHeightDp
21	    val itemHeightDp = 80
22	
23	    val shimmerCount = remember { (screenHeightDp / itemHeightDp).toInt() }
24	
25	    LazyColumn {
26	        items(shimmerCount) { ShimmerItem() }
27	    }
28	}
29	```
30	
31	After rotation, `screenHeightDp` changes but `shimmerCount` still holds the portrait value. The list renders the wrong number of shimmer placeholders. In extreme cases (foldable unfolding), the stale count causes layout overflow or zero items.
32	
33	### Fix
34	
35	```kotlin
36	// GOOD: screenHeightDp is a key, so remember recalculates on config change
37	@Composable
38	fun ShimmerList() {
39	    val config = LocalConfiguration.current
40	    val screenHeightDp = config.screenHeightDp
41	    val itemHeightDp = 80
42	
43	    val shimmerCount = remember(screenHeightDp) {
44	        (screenHeightDp / itemHeightDp).toInt().coerceAtLeast(1)
45	    }
46	
47	    LazyColumn {
48	        items(shimmerCount) { ShimmerItem() }
49	    }
50	}
51	```
52	
53	**Rule:** Any value derived from `LocalConfiguration`, `LocalDensity`, or `LocalLayoutDirection` MUST include that configuration source in `remember`'s key parameters. Audit all `remember {}` calls that reference `screenHeightDp`, `screenWidthDp`, `fontScale`, or `densityDpi`.
54	
55	### Compose Multiplatform — `LocalConfiguration` Is Android-Only
56	
57	`LocalConfiguration` does not exist in `commonMain`. To derive layout dimensions in shared CMP code, read `LocalWindowInfo.current.containerSize` (an `IntSize` in pixels) and convert with `LocalDensity.current`:
58	
59	```kotlin
60	// commonMain — works on Android, iOS, Desktop, Web
61	@Composable
62	fun ResponsiveShimmerList(itemHeightDp: Int = 80) {
63	    val containerSize = LocalWindowInfo.current.containerSize  // IntSize in pixels
64	    val density = LocalDensity.current
65	    val screenHeightDp = with(density) { containerSize.height.toDp().value.toInt() }
66	
67	    val shimmerCount = remember(screenHeightDp) {
68	        (screenHeightDp / itemHeightDp).coerceAtLeast(1)
69	    }
70	
71	    LazyColumn { items(shimmerCount) { ShimmerItem() } }
72	}
73	```
74	
75	`LocalWindowInfo` is multiplatform from `compose.ui:ui` 1.6+ — the same crash pattern applies (rotate or resize the window without keying, the shimmer count goes stale), with the same fix shape (key on the derived value).

79	## 2. indexOf() Inside items {}
80	
81	### Root Cause
82	
83	Using `list.indexOf(item)` inside a LazyColumn's `items {}` block is O(n) per item, making the overall list O(n^2). Worse, `indexOf` uses structural equality (`equals`). If the list contains recreated objects (new instances from a network response mapped to data classes), `indexOf` may return `-1`, which when passed as an index triggers `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.
84	
85	### Crash Pattern
86	
87	```kotlin
88	// BAD: O(n^2) and crashes when indexOf returns -1
89	@Composable
90	fun MessageList(messages: List<Message>) {
91	    LazyColumn {
92	        items(messages) { message ->
93	            val index = messages.indexOf(message)  // O(n) per item
94	            MessageRow(
95	                message = message,
96	                isEven = index % 2 == 0  // -1 % 2 == -1, not a crash here
97	            )
98	        }
99	    }
100	}
101	
102	// Worse: using indexOf result as a direct index
103	items(messages) { message ->
104	    val index = messages.indexOf(message)
105	    val nextMessage = messages[index + 1]  // IndexOutOfBoundsException
106	}
107	```
108	
109	### Fix
110	
111	```kotlin
112	// GOOD: Use itemsIndexed to get the index directly
113	@Composable
114	fun MessageList(messages: List<Message>) {
115	    LazyColumn {
116	        itemsIndexed(
117	            items = messages,
118	            key = { _, message -> message.id }
119	        ) { index, message ->
120	            MessageRow(
121	                message = message,
122	                isEven = index % 2 == 0
123	            )
124	        }
125	    }
126	}
127	```
128	
129	If you need `items` with a key but also need the index, use `items` with `key` and derive the index from the item itself if possible, or switch to `itemsIndexed`.
130	
131	**Rule:** Never call `indexOf()`, `lastIndexOf()`, or `indexOfFirst {}` inside a `LazyListScope` item factory. Use `itemsIndexed` for index access. Use `items(key = { ... })` for stable identity.

135	## 3. DrawScope Without Zero-Size Guard
136	
137	### Root Cause
138	
139	During initial composition, a `Canvas` composable may receive a `Size.Zero` (or `Size.Unspecified`) before layout completes, especially when using `fillMaxSize()` inside a parent that hasn't been measured yet. Dividing by zero-dimension values or computing radii from `size.minDimension` when it's zero produces `NaN` or `Infinity`, which crashes the Skia rendering pipeline.
140	
141	### Crash Pattern
142	
143	```kotlin
144	// BAD: size.minDimension is 0 during initial composition
145	Canvas(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
146	    val radius = size.minDimension / 2
147	    drawCircle(color = Color.Blue, radius = radius)
148	}
149	```
150	
151	On certain devices or inside `SubcomposeLayout`, the first draw call fires with `size = Size(0, 0)`. The `drawCircle` call with `radius = 0f` may not crash, but derived math like `360f / size.width` produces `Infinity` and corrupts the draw path.
152	
153	### Fix
154	
155	```kotlin
156	// GOOD: guard against zero size, and give Canvas an explicit size
157	Canvas(
158	    modifier = Modifier
159	        .fillMaxWidth()
160	        .height(200.dp)
161	) {
162	    if (size.minDimension <= 0f) return@Canvas
163	    val radius = size.minDimension / 2
164	    drawCircle(color = Color.Blue, radius = radius)
165	}
166	```
167	
168	For dynamic sizing, use `Modifier.aspectRatio()` or `BoxWithConstraints` to guarantee non-zero dimensions before drawing:
169	
170	```kotlin
171	BoxWithConstraints(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
172	    if (maxWidth > 0.dp && maxHeight > 0.dp) {
173	        Canvas(modifier = Modifier.size(maxWidth, maxWidth)) {
174	            val radius = size.minDimension / 2
175	            drawCircle(color = Color.Blue, radius = radius)
176	        }
177	    }
178	}
179	```
180	
181	**Rule:** Always guard `DrawScope` blocks against zero-size conditions. Never use `fillMaxSize()` on `Canvas` without an explicit height constraint. Prefer `Modifier.size()`, `Modifier.height()`, or `Modifier.aspectRatio()` so Canvas always enters draw with known dimensions.

185	## 4. Duplicate LazyColumn Keys
186	
187	### Root Cause
188	
189	`LazyColumn` requires unique keys across all items. When the backend sends items without unique IDs, or when a WebSocket reconnection delivers duplicate messages before deduplication, duplicate keys cause `IllegalArgumentException: Key ... was already used`.
190	
191	### Crash Pattern
192	
193	```kotlin
194	// BAD: backend sends duplicate IDs after WebSocket reconnect
195	data class Notification(val id: String, val text: String)
196	
197	LazyColumn {
198	    items(
199	        items = notifications,
200	        key = { it.id }  // Crashes if two items share the same id
201	    ) { notification ->
202	        NotificationRow(notification)
203	    }
204	}
205	```
206	
207	### Fix: Dedup Index Pattern
208	
209	Add a `dedupIndex` field that is excluded from `equals`/`hashCode` but included in the key. This handles duplicates gracefully without losing data:
210	
211	```kotlin
212	data class Notification(
213	    val id: String,
214	    val text: String,
215	    val timestamp: Long
216	) {
217	    // dedupIndex is NOT in the primary constructor, excluded from equals/hashCode
218	    var dedupIndex: Int = 0
219	}
220	
221	fun List<Notification>.withDedupIndex(): List<Notification> {
222	    val seen = mutableMapOf<String, Int>()
223	    return map { item ->
224	        val count = seen.getOrDefault(item.id, 0)
225	        seen[item.id] = count + 1
226	        item.also { it.dedupIndex = count }
227	    }
228	}
229	
230	@Composable
231	fun NotificationList(notifications: List<Notification>) {
232	    val deduped = remember(notifications) { notifications.withDedupIndex() }
233	
234	    LazyColumn {
235	        items(
236	            items = deduped,
237	            key = { "${it.id}_${it.dedupIndex}" }  // Guaranteed unique
238	        ) { notification ->
239	            NotificationRow(notification)
240	        }
241	    }
242	}
243	```
244	
245	An alternative defensive approach using `distinctBy` when true duplicates should be dropped:
246	
247	```kotlin
248	val uniqueNotifications = remember(notifications) {
249	    notifications.distinctBy { it.id }
250	}
251	```
252	
253	**Rule:** Never trust backend data to provide unique keys. Either deduplicate with `distinctBy` or use the dedup-index pattern to make keys unique. Wrap key construction in a function that can be unit-tested.

257	## 5. derivedStateOf Driving Collection Size
258	
259	### Root Cause
260	
261	`derivedStateOf` recalculates lazily when its inputs change, but the recomposition that reads the derived value and the recomposition that reads the source collection may occur in different frames. When `derivedStateOf` exposes only a count, the `items(count)` call may use a stale count that is out of sync with the actual collection, causing `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.
262	
263	### Crash Pattern
264	
265	```kotlin
266	// BAD: derive only the count; items {} reads allItems directly with stale count
267	@Composable
268	fun FilteredList(allItems: List<Item>, filter: String) {
269	    val itemCount by remember {
270	        derivedStateOf { allItems.count { it.name.contains(filter) } }
271	    }
272	
273	    LazyColumn {
274	        items(itemCount) { index ->
275	            val item = allItems.filter { it.name.contains(filter) }[index]
276	            // itemCount may be stale relative to allItems, IOOB crash
277	            ItemRow(item)
278	        }
279	    }
280	}
281	```
282	
283	### Fix
284	
285	```kotlin
286	// GOOD: derive the full filtered list; count and access are always consistent
287	@Composable
288	fun FilteredList(allItems: List<Item>, filter: String) {
289	    val filteredItems by remember {
290	        derivedStateOf { allItems.filter { it.name.contains(filter) } }
291	    }
292	
293	    LazyColumn {
294	        items(
295	            items = filteredItems,
296	            key = { it.id }
297	        ) { item ->
298	            ItemRow(item)
299	        }
300	    }
301	}
302	```
303	
304	**Rule:** `derivedStateOf` is appropriate for scroll direction, visibility thresholds, and validation states -- values that don't drive collection iteration. Never use `derivedStateOf` to expose a count or index that a `LazyList` will use to access a separate collection.

308	## 6. collectAsState vs collectAsStateWithLifecycle
309	
310	### Root Cause
311	
312	`collectAsState()` subscribes to a `Flow` and keeps collecting even when the app is in the background. This causes unnecessary work (network calls, database queries, sensor reads), battery drain, and stale state that flashes briefly when the user returns to the app.
313	
314	### The Difference
315	
316	```kotlin
317	// BAD: continues collecting in background
318	@Composable
319	fun ProfileScreen(viewModel: ProfileViewModel) {
320	    val state by viewModel.uiState.collectAsState()
321	    ProfileContent(state)
322	}
323	
324	// GOOD: stops collecting when lifecycle drops below STARTED
325	@Composable
326	fun ProfileScreen(viewModel: ProfileViewModel) {
327	    val state by viewModel.uiState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
328	    ProfileContent(state)
329	}
330	```
331	
332	`collectAsStateWithLifecycle` is part of `androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-runtime-compose`. It automatically cancels collection when the `Lifecycle` drops below a configurable state (default: `Lifecycle.State.STARTED`).
333	
334	### Custom Lifecycle Minimum
335	
336	```kotlin
337	// Collect only when RESUMED (stricter, for camera/location flows)
338	val locationState by locationFlow.collectAsStateWithLifecycle(
339	    minActiveState = Lifecycle.State.RESUMED
340	)
341	```
342	
343	### Compose Multiplatform Consideration
344	
345	`collectAsStateWithLifecycle` is Android-only because it depends on `androidx.lifecycle`. In Compose Multiplatform (CMP) projects, use `collectAsState()` on non-Android targets and `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` on Android via an `expect`/`actual` pattern:
346	
347	```kotlin
348	// commonMain
349	@Composable
350	expect fun <T> Flow<T>.collectAsStateMultiplatform(
351	    initial: T
352	): State<T>
353	
354	// androidMain
355	@Composable
356	actual fun <T> Flow<T>.collectAsStateMultiplatform(
357	    initial: T
358	): State<T> = collectAsStateWithLifecycle(initialValue = initial)
359	
360	// iosMain / desktopMain / wasmJsMain
361	@Composable
362	actual fun <T> Flow<T>.collectAsStateMultiplatform(
363	    initial: T
364	): State<T> = collectAsState(initial = initial)
365	```
366	
367	**Rule:** On Android, always use `collectAsStateWithLifecycle` for `StateFlow` and `SharedFlow`. Reserve `collectAsState` for Compose Multiplatform common code or non-lifecycle-aware contexts only.

371	## 7. SafeShimmerItem Pattern
372	
373	### Root Cause
374	
375	Shimmer placeholders rendered via `SubcomposeLayout` can crash when the parent layout has zero size (see Section 3) or when the shimmer animation's `DrawScope` receives unexpected dimensions. A defensive wrapper prevents crashes while maintaining the shimmer UX.
376	
377	### Full Implementation
378	
379	```kotlin
380	@Composable
381	fun SafeShimmerItem(
382	    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
383	    itemHeight: Dp = 80.dp,
384	    shimmerColor: Color = Color.LightGray.copy(alpha = 0.6f),
385	    highlightColor: Color = Color.LightGray.copy(alpha = 0.2f),
386	) {
387	    val transition = rememberInfiniteTransition(label = "shimmer")
388	    val translateAnim by transition.animateFloat(
389	        initialValue = 0f,
390	        targetValue = 1000f,
391	        animationSpec = infiniteRepeatable(
392	            animation = tween(durationMillis = 1200, easing = LinearEasing),
393	            repeatMode = RepeatMode.Restart
394	        ),
395	        label = "shimmer_translate"
396	    )
397	
398	    val brush = Brush.linearGradient(
399	        colors = listOf(shimmerColor, highlightColor, shimmerColor),
400	        start = Offset(translateAnim - 500f, 0f),
401	        end = Offset(translateAnim, 0f)
402	    )
403	
404	    Box(
405	        modifier = modifier
406	            .fillMaxWidth()
407	            .height(itemHeight)
408	            .clip(RoundedCornerShape(8.dp))
409	    ) {
410	        val result = runCatching {
411	            Canvas(modifier = Modifier.matchParentSize()) {
412	                if (size.minDimension <= 0f) return@Canvas
413	                drawRect(brush = brush)
414	            }
415	        }
416	        if (result.isFailure) {
417	            // Fallback: solid color placeholder when Canvas fails
418	            Box(
419	                modifier = Modifier
420	                    .matchParentSize()
421	                    .background(shimmerColor, RoundedCornerShape(8.dp))
422	            )
423	        }
424	    }
425	}
426	```
427	
428	### Usage with Configuration-Aware Count
429	
430	```kotlin
431	@Composable
432	fun ShimmerLoadingList() {
433	    val config = LocalConfiguration.current
434	    val itemHeight = 80.dp
435	    val shimmerCount = remember(config.screenHeightDp) {
436	        (config.screenHeightDp / itemHeight.value).toInt().coerceAtLeast(1)
437	    }
438	
439	    LazyColumn {
440	        items(shimmerCount) {
441	            SafeShimmerItem(itemHeight = itemHeight)
442	        }
443	    }
444	}
445	```
446	
447	**Rule:** Wrap all shimmer and placeholder drawing in `try/catch` or explicit size guards. Provide a solid-color fallback so the loading state is never invisible and never crashes. Avoid `runCatching` in suspend contexts — it catches `CancellationException` and breaks structured concurrency.

451	## 8. Multi-Field Keys with Collision Prefixes
452	
453	### Root Cause
454	
455	When a `LazyColumn` displays items from multiple categories (live, archived, pinned), using the raw ID as the key causes collisions when the same underlying entity appears in multiple sections. For example, a message with `id = 42` could appear in both "pinned" and "live" sections.
456	
457	### Crash Pattern
458	
459	```kotlin
460	// BAD: same message ID in pinned and live sections causes key collision
461	LazyColumn {
462	    items(pinnedMessages, key = { it.id }) { message ->
463	        PinnedMessageRow(message)
464	    }
465	    items(liveMessages, key = { it.id }) { message ->
466	        LiveMessageRow(message)
467	    }
468	}
469	// IllegalArgumentException: Key 42 was already used
470	```
471	
472	### Fix: Type-Prefixed Keys
473	
474	```kotlin
475	// GOOD: prefix keys with section type to avoid collisions
476	LazyColumn {
477	    items(
478	        items = pinnedMessages,
479	        key = { "pinned_${it.id}" }
480	    ) { message ->
481	        PinnedMessageRow(message)
482	    }
483	    items(
484	        items = liveMessages,
485	        key = { "live_${it.id}" }
486	    ) { message ->
487	        LiveMessageRow(message)
488	    }
489	    items(
490	        items = archivedMessages,
491	        key = { "archived_${it.id}" }
492	    ) { message ->
493	        ArchivedMessageRow(message)
494	    }
495	}
496	```
497	
498	### Sealed Class Alternative
499	
500	For type safety, use a sealed class for keys:
501	
502	```kotlin
503	sealed class ListKey {
504	    data class Pinned(val id: Long) : ListKey()
505	    data class Live(val id: Long) : ListKey()
506	    data class Archived(val id: Long) : ListKey()
507	}
508	
509	LazyColumn {
510	    items(pinnedMessages, key = { ListKey.Pinned(it.id) }) { ... }
511	    items(liveMessages, key = { ListKey.Live(it.id) }) { ... }
512	    items(archivedMessages, key = { ListKey.Archived(it.id) }) { ... }
513	}
514	```
515	
516	**Rule:** When mixing item types in a single `LazyList`, always prefix or wrap keys with the item type. Use string prefixes for simplicity or sealed classes for compile-time safety.

520	## 9. Per-Item `rememberSaveable` → `TransactionTooLargeException`
521	
522	`rememberSaveable` serializes to the `Bundle`, which round-trips through binder for `onSaveInstanceState` — and binder enforces a ~1MB IPC transaction limit. Using it for per-item state inside a `LazyColumn` packs every item's value into that one Bundle, blows past the limit, and crashes.
523	
524	```kotlin
525	// BAD — saved for every message in the list; Bundle size explodes -> TransactionTooLargeException
526	LazyColumn {
527	    items(messages, key = { it.id }) { message ->
528	        var expanded by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }   // ✗ per-item saved state
529	    }
530	}
531	
532	// GOOD — rememberSaveable at screen level, plain remember inside items
533	var searchQuery by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("") }           // screen-level: fine
534	LazyColumn {
535	    items(messages, key = { it.id }) { message ->
536	        var expanded by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }           // per-item: plain remember
537	    }
538	}
539	```
540	
541	The mechanism: `rememberSaveable` writes to a `SaveableStateRegistry`; at save time the registry packs every registered value into the `Bundle` that binder round-trips for `onSaveInstanceState`, and binder enforces the ~1MB limit.
542	
543	**Compose Multiplatform:** the binder ~1MB limit is Android-only (Desktop/iOS serialize to other storage), but the per-item rule holds everywhere — per-item saved state scales linearly with list size, defeats recycling, and pollutes saved state with values that should be hoisted or derived.
544	
545	> The other "production state rules" once listed here — `mutableStateOf` belongs in composables not ViewModels; `Channel` vs `SharedFlow` for one-shot events; `snapshotFlow + distinctUntilChanged` for reactive scroll; `stateIn + map` for derived flows — are general state/flow guidance rather than crash patterns, and live in their canonical homes: `android-skills:kotlin-flows` and `compose/references/state-management.md`.

1	# Compose State Management
2	
3	This reference covers the state traps and boundaries, not the basics of `mutableStateOf` / `remember` / hoisting / `derivedStateOf`.
4	
5	## The unified keying rule
6	
7	`remember`, `LaunchedEffect`, `DisposableEffect`, `produceState`, and the `remember { }` around `derivedStateOf` share one rule: **any changing value the body reads must either be in the key list, be a constant, be a call-site-owned stable object, or be read through `rememberUpdatedState`.** The three legitimate carve-outs:
8	
9	1. **Constants** — `MAX_RETRY = 3`, `Color.Red`.
10	2. **Call-site-owned stable objects the call site never replaces** — `rememberCoroutineScope()`, `remember { Animatable(0f) }`; the key would be redundant.
11	3. **Initial-only capture is the goal** — `val firstSeenAt = remember { Clock.System.now() }`; mark it `// initial-only` so the missing key doesn't read as a bug.
12	
13	For a value that should keep an effect *running* across changes but invoke the *latest* callback (e.g. `onComplete`), wrap it with `rememberUpdatedState(value)` and read inside the effect — it tracks the latest without restarting.
14	
15	## Don't `rememberSaveable` a runtime object
16	
17	`rememberSaveable` serializes *data*; runtime references (`LazyListState`, `FocusRequester`, `CoroutineScope`, callbacks) don't survive process death. Persist the data and recreate the object:
18	
19	```kotlin
20	// WRONG — runtime object, no meaningful serialization
21	val listState = rememberSaveable { LazyListState() }
22	
23	// RIGHT — save the index, recreate the state
24	var savedIndex by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
25	val listState = rememberLazyListState(initialFirstVisibleItemIndex = savedIndex)
26	LaunchedEffect(listState) { snapshotFlow { listState.firstVisibleItemIndex }.collect { savedIndex = it } }
27	```

29	## A UI value that drives business logic belongs in the ViewModel
30	
31	The hoisting boundary isn't "is this UI?" — it's "does my repository or navigation graph depend on this value?" A search query that feeds repository queries is the canonical case:
32	
33	```kotlin
34	// WRONG — query is UI-local, but every keystroke hits the repo: can't debounce, restore, or test
35	var query by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
36	LaunchedEffect(query) { viewModel.search(query) }
37	
38	// RIGHT — query lives in the VM, which owns debouncing + the repository call
39	class SearchViewModel : ViewModel() {
40	    private val _query = MutableStateFlow("")
41	    val results = _query.debounce(300)
42	        .flatMapLatest { repository.search(it) }   // mapLatest if search() is a suspend fun returning the list
43	        .stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5000), emptyList())
44	    fun onQueryChange(new: String) { _query.value = new }
45	}
46	```

48	## `derivedStateOf` + the surrounding `remember` capture trap
49

bugVerdicts.description: rcosteira performance.md GOOD example `remember(items, query) { derivedStateOf { items.filter { query in it.title } } }` wraps plain values in derivedStateOf for no benefit.

bugVerdicts.description: rcosteira production-crash-playbook.md §7 SafeShimmerItem wraps a composable Canvas in runCatching, which cannot catch the draw-phase crash it targets.

bugVerdicts.description: rcosteira production-crash-playbook.md §4 dedup-index mutates caller-owned data and collides on same-instance duplicates.
bugVerdicts.reasoning: Verified lines 212-243. `Notification` has a mutable `var dedupIndex` outside the constructor, and `withDedupIndex()` returns `item.also { it.dedupIndex = count }` — a purported pure transform that mutates the caller's original instances in place (the returned list holds the same references as the input).
